descriptionHtml:
Bug B26 · P1 · known

The Bedrock guardrail version is not pinned: infra publishes no numbered version and the code defaults to DRAFT (UAT 3.1 asks to record the guardrail version)

Tickets: TFA-94422 ready for qa; TFA-94059 in progress · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local (code review)

Approach · OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · S23 Mistral goes through the same Bedrock guardrail as Haiku

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U6 The Mistral call goes through the same Bedrock guardrail as Haiku (UAT OAT-03 Expected Result 3; TFA-94422 AC 4)
  • U6b Every AI call (including Ask AI, handoff, photo reading and voice transcription) leaves from the server with the guardrail applied (TFA-92568 AC 13) — gate: blocked: TFA-92568 in progress

Test design technique: Equivalence classes (equivalence) — Check the same rule again with another class of input (Hospital / Nursing Home, other data); every class has to be right.

Given Code at origin/main e02167f; the UAT deployment's guardrail id / version from Tim's 3.1 build record (never read env from )

When Read convex/ai/providers/bedrock.ts (invoke), convex/ai/providers/index.ts (chat, vision), convex/ai/transcribe.ts and infra/stacks/aws.ts (IAM policy); take the guardrail id / version from Tim's 3.1 build record

Then U6: primary and fallback are sent through the same invoke with the same guardrailConfig (id and version); the IAM policy denies any invocation without a guardrail; the guardrail version is pinned (not DRAFT) where UAT runs (ties to OAT-05 step 7). …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Document review with file/line evidence. U6 is judged now (TFA-94422 AC 4). The vision / transcription gap is recorded against U6b, which is gated (TFA-92568 in progress), so it reports as Blocked, not as a Fail of OAT-03 Expected Result 3. A guardrail that masks or blocks returns a normal response and never triggers the fallback (Q7); …

Where it ran: local code-review (judged by reading the code); test method CODEREVIEW · Code review; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S23 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-03.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Known product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92568 in progress; TFA-94422 ready for qa; TFA-94059 in progress

Nothing a physician sees: Haiku and Mistral go through the same Bedrock guardrail, but its version is not pinned, because the infra stack publishes no numbered version and the code falls back to the working DRAFT.

Evidence: allure 0e0bda86-…-result.json; code-review/OAT-03-S23.json. Pins: bedrock.ts:123-124 (the code default is DRAFT), infra/stacks/aws.ts:118/197 (no GuardrailVersion; it exports guardrail.version), .github/workflows/infra.yml:238 (the export is copied into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION). Treated as known because the OAT-05 matrix already notes the DRAFT default and TFA-94059 AC 'Guardrail config and model ID are pinned in prod and match what UAT ran on' (in progress) covers exactly this. OAT-05 Q6 asks whether DRAFT counts as pinned, and the deployed id/version is in Tim's 3.1 record. U6b (photo, voice and OpenAI text bypass the guardrail) is gated on TFA-92568.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane code-review.

Test method: CODEREVIEW · Code review; secondary: CONFIG · Config check — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: code-review.

UAT item: OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-03/S23

Mistral goes through the same Bedrock guardrail as Haiku

Tickets: TFA-92568 Phase 4: Make it safe for real patients (in progress); TFA-94422 Haiku primary, Mistral fallback via Bedrock (ready for qa)

New local lane code-review: status failed in code-review/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact)).

Detail:

Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.

Product issue (from physicianImpact): the lane wrote no productIssue; "failed · product" is counted from its physicianImpact (full text below).

New findings (newFindings):

  • apps/web/convex/ai/providers/bedrock.ts:123: invoke adds guardrailConfig from env for every model; when BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION is unset the code sends DRAFT.
  • infra/stacks/aws.ts:197: The stack creates only a Guardrail resource (no published GuardrailVersion), and exports guardrail.version, which is the working DRAFT for an unpublished guardrail.
  • infra/stacks/aws.ts:118: The Guardrail resource definition; there is no aws.bedrock.GuardrailVersion in infra/.
  • apps/web/convex/ai/providers/bedrock.ts:124: If BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION is unset, the code sends the unpinned DRAFT version
  • infra/stacks/aws.ts:118: Only a Guardrail resource is created; there is no GuardrailVersion resource, so no numbered version is published
  • infra/stacks/aws.ts:197: The stack exports the Guardrail resource's own version (the working draft) as guardrailVersion

Differs from the Then (againstThen):

  • .github/workflows/infra.yml:238: The infra workflow copies the exported stack version into the Convex env, so a DRAFT export becomes the version the app sends.
  • apps/web/convex/ai/providers/index.ts:259: Photo reading goes to Vertex or to OpenAI vision, never through the Bedrock guardrail.
  • apps/web/convex/ai/providers/index.ts:198: Text chat can be sent to OpenAI (when the provider is not bedrock) without the Bedrock guardrail.
  • apps/web/convex/ai/transcribe.ts:12: Transcription calls the OpenAI audio endpoint directly, with no Bedrock guardrail.
  • .github/workflows/infra.yml:238: The infra workflow writes that exported version into the Convex env BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION
  • apps/web/convex/ai/providers/index.ts:259: Photo reading goes to Vertex (or OpenAI vision) and never through the Bedrock guardrail
  • apps/web/convex/ai/transcribe.ts:12: Transcription posts audio straight to OpenAI, outside the Bedrock guardrail
  • apps/web/convex/ai/providers/index.ts:197: An operator can switch text generation to OpenAI, which then bypasses the Bedrock guardrail

Open questions (openQuestions):

  • The question says pass if the stack publishes a pinned version. The oracle ties that to Tim's 3.1 build record and OAT-05 step 7. If UAT's BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION was set by hand to a published number, the deployment could be pinned even though the code exports DRAFT and falls back to DRAFT. The code fail stands either way.
  • The scenario's Then makes the DRAFT check a config item for the deployed build (Tim's 3.1 record, OAT-05 step 7). The question's fail rule also fails a DRAFT export or a DRAFT code fallback, and that is what I applied. If the deployed build pins a numbered version by hand, U6 can pass on the deployment, but the stack and code still default to DRAFT.
  • Should the IAM Deny check the specific guardrail ARN or version, not just that some guardrail is present? As written, any guardrail id satisfies it.

Not decidable from the code (notDecidableByCode):

  • deployed guardrail id/version (CONFIG (Tim's 3.1 record))
  • U6b (gated on TFA-92568: reported as Blocked)
  • The actual guardrail id and version set on the UAT deployment (Tim's 3.1 build record)
  • That Pulumi's aws.bedrock.Guardrail 'version' output is 'DRAFT' for an unpublished guardrail is the provider's behaviour, not code in this repo
  • Whether the IAM Null-condition deny is enforced for Converse calls in the deployed account
  • Which guardrail id and version the UAT deployment actually has set in BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID and BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION (Tim's 3.1 build record)
  • Whether aws.bedrock.Guardrail.version resolves to DRAFT at runtime. That comes from AWS/Pulumi behaviour, not this repo, though CreateGuardrail normally returns DRAFT
  • Whether the Converse API call is checked against the bedrock:InvokeModel IAM action and the bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier condition key in the deployed account

Physician impact (physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

Review verdict (verdict): fail

Evidence: 2 attached.

Dev run: skipped: not runnable on dev — not-runnable-on-dev: outside-runner (manual: doc-review). This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
